# Problem 0

## Loading All Libraries

```{r loading_libraries, message = F}
# loading tidyverse library
library(tidyverse)

# loading p8105.datasets library
library(p8105.datasets)
```


# Problem 1

## Reading ny_noaa dataset

```{r reading_p1_data, message = F}
# reading ny_noaa data
data("ny_noaa")
```

## Short Description

The `ny_noaa` has `r nrow(ny_noaa)` rows and `r ncol(ny_noaa)` columns. Its key (column) variables include `r paste(names(ny_noaa), collapse = ", ")`. The variables have the following data types, respectively: `r paste(sapply(ny_noaa, class), collapse = ", ")`. As for what each variable represents: `id` gives the weather station ID, 
`date` gives the date of observation, `prcp` gives precipitation in tenths of mm, `snow` gives snowfall in mm, `snwd` gives snow depth in mm, `tmax` gives maximum temperature in tenths of degrees C, and `tmin` gives minimum temperature in tenths of degrees C. The proportion of missing values in each column is approximately as follows: `r ny_noaa |> summarize(across(everything(), ~ mean(is.na(.x)) * 100)) |> round(2) |> paste0("%", collapse = ", ")`. To clean the data, the missing values should be standardized to `NA`.

## Cleaning ny_noaa Data

```{r ny_noaa_data_cleaning, message = F}
# creating, cleaning and standardizing values in ny_noaa_df
ny_noaa_df =
  ny_noaa |>
  separate(date, into = c("year", "month", "day"), sep = "-") |>
mutate(
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10,
    prcp = as.numeric(prcp) / 10
  )

# counting the most commonly observed values for snowfall
ny_noaa_df |>
  count(snow, sort = TRUE) |>
  head(10)
```

## Interpretation

In the `ny_noaa_df`, `r ny_noaa |> summarize(median_snow = median(snow, na.rm = TRUE))`mm is the most commonly observed value because it does not snow throughout most of the year in New York.
